63: // diff compares two multi-line strings and returns a helpful comment
64: func diff(got, want string) string {
65: 	g := strings.Split(got, "\n")
66: 	w := strings.Split(want, "\n")
67: 	for i := 0; ; i++ {
68: 		switch {
69: 		case i < len(g) && i < len(w):
70: 			if g[i] == w[i] {
71: 				continue
72: 			}
73: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- first difference in line %d:\n"+
74: 				"-- got : %q\n-- want: %q\n", i+1, g[i], w[i])
75: 		case i < len(g):
76: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d extra lines after line %d:\n"+
77: 				"-- first extra line: %q\n", len(g)-len(w), i, g[i])
78: 		case i < len(w):
79: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d correct lines, want %d more lines:\n"+
80: 				"-- want next: %q\n", i, len(w)-i, w[i])
81: 		default:
82: 			return "no differences found"
83: 		}
84: 	}
85: }

All tests pass. The implementation in `food_chain.go` builds the song algorithmically from two tables:

- **`creatures`** — the eight animals in order (fly → horse)
- **`comments`** — each animal's second line (the spider's wriggle line, "How absurd...", etc.)

`Verse(v)` emits the "I know an old lady..." line, the comment, then walks the chain backwards — "She swallowed the X to catch the Y" — appending "that wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her" when catching the spider, and closing with the fly's "Perhaps she'll die" line. The fly verse (v=1) and horse verse (v=8) skip the chain entirely. `Verses` joins a range of verses with blank lines, and `Song` is `Verses(1, 8)`.
